reason: The digestive tube has a named portal vessel slot, and the vessel connects the intestine to the liver.
expectation: The portal vessel will fit into the digestive tube and connect the gut to the liver.

effect: The portal vessel is fitted, completing the visible digestive-tube slots.
reaction: The named slot made that connection straightforward.
reason: The liver tissue and glycogen-making enzymes suggest a way to begin storing the meal's glucose.
expectation: The enzymes will prepare the liver tissue to make glycogen from glucose.

alternatives.reason: The nutrients could first enter the liver tissue before storage.

effect: The liver first receives the portal nutrients; I can now try the glycogen-making enzymes on it.
reaction: The compatibility feedback clarified the order.
reason: The liver now has access to glucose, and the enzymes link glucose into glycogen.
expectation: The liver will store some of the glucose as glycogen.

effect: The liver has stored glucose as glycogen; the remaining goal also calls for its release.
reaction: The result clearly connects glucose storage with glycogen.
reason: The glycogen-release enzymes are the visible counterpart to the enzymes used for storage.
expectation: The liver will release glucose from its stored glycogen.

effect: The liver is releasing glucose from glycogen; blood transport may carry it away.
reaction: The storage and release sequence is easy to follow.
reason: The blood transport item shows a vessel carrying blood away from liver tissue.
expectation: The released glucose will enter blood leaving the liver.

effect: Glucose is now available in blood, completing the storage and release goal. The digestive system still needs to connect to the moving body.
reaction: The result makes the purpose of liver glucose storage clear.
reason: The supplied movement model represents the body’s circulation, and the completed digestive tube has the portal route fitted.
expectation: The digestive system will connect to the movement model’s circulation.

effect: The digestive system is connected to the body model, completing the chapter's remaining goal.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the digestive organs join the larger circulation, though the final connection was predictable.

mostWorthwhile.text: The storage and release sequence was most worthwhile: it showed glucose becoming glycogen, then returning to the blood for other tissues to use.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting the named portal vessel into its slot was clear but offered little to figure out.

surprise.text: I expected to add the glycogen-making enzymes to liver tissue first. The compatibility feedback showed that the liver needed to receive portal nutrients before storage.

arbitrary.text: The required order initially felt a little arbitrary because I expected the enzymes could prepare the liver before nutrients arrived. The feedback made the intended sequence clear.

continue.text: I would be interested in another chapter if it continued connecting the systems and explaining their effects. This chapter's storage and release sequence was clear, although most choices were predictable.
